items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: some player that I had borrowed from Frankie © Fillius Jazz Archive -12- Capp’s band, who was going to be sitting in my band

ctx.x: Yeah. About my big band. That we had showed up to play somewhere and another band was up there playing and my music had been taken off the stand and taken somewhere else, and no one would tell me where it went. And my wife Mary Ann was there and she was angry about the whole thing, and some player that I had borrowed from Frankie © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

Capp’s band, who was going to be sitting in my band, did this thing. It was just a weird, weird dream. I can’t imagine why it came, because I haven’t even thought about my big band in a while. We play so seldom. We played down at the IAJE this year in Anaheim, and it was a rousing success. They couldn’t get all the people in the room that they wanted to get in there to hear it.
